content.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   windows     build-windows.yml windows-x64 app zip (fa-app-windows-x64.zip,
#                                 stable name), attached to the next-tag
#                                 release — the Windows counterpart of the
#                                 TestFlight leg: one release-quality GUI
#                                 app build per day (gh-2140)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - windows
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - windows
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, wait for it read-only, fail on any non-success conclusion.
  # The child run URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt
  # its log.
  #
  # ── The gh-1903 invariant: queued on the single self-hosted runner is
  # HEALTHY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # dispatch_and_watch.sh NEVER cancels or re-dispatches a child mid-watch.
  # A child queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is normal
  # operation; the old #344 budget + gh-172 queue-stall watchdog cancelled
  # two such healthy queued children on 2026-10-26 (daily run 40274465122,
  # tracking issue #1735 — those cancellations were THIS defect, not an
  # ASC/IPA problem) and failed a fully-built v1.0.648 solely by killing
  # its place in line. What bounds a slow child instead:
  #   * every job in a watched child chain carries an explicit
  #     timeout-minutes — a wedged self-hosted job self-fails server-side
  #     (#344; a job-level timeout is enforced BY the runner, which is why
  #     a hung worker outliving its own ceiling is the one class the
  #     server cannot kill), and
  #   * the leg timeout-minutes below — when it fires, the runner TERMs
  #     the watcher, which cancels ONLY this leg's own NEVER-STARTED child
  #     (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) so an orphaned queued run cannot publish
  #     unattended, then fails naming the child run, its last observed
  #     state, and the observed pool activity (gh-172 diagnostic).
  # While the child has not started, the watcher logs sibling in-progress
  # runs on a diagnostic interval — read-only; cannot-observe ⇒
  # cannot-judge ⇒ never a cancel.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351, leg-timeout sizing) ────────────────────────
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Invariant: leg timeout > child worst-case +
  # margin (appear window 60×10s ≈ 10m + poll slack ≈ 5m) — the leg always
  # outlives a healthy slow child, which is now NEVER killed.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  ;  360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   ;  240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  ;  360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases grew by exactly the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   ;  180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   ;  150m
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20) history: the re-dispatched
  # testflight child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker —
  # the leg burned its remaining ~107m and died as a bare 360m ceiling
  # kill with no diagnosis. The budget/stall watchdog built to catch that
  # faster could not tell a zombie-held pool from a sibling leg's job
  # legitimately occupying the shared fa-m5-1 (its own comment admitted
  # it), and its 31m stall window did not cover the cli sibling chain's
  # 335m worst-case — so it false-cancelled healthy queues by design
  # (gh-1903, #1735). The zombie goal is now met by the bounds above plus
  # the leg-timeout orphan-cancel diagnostic, not by a heuristic that
  # cannot tell a queue from a zombie.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120); 360m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. The 360m cap
    # also bounds any gh-172 zombie wait — on leg timeout the watcher's
    # orphan-cancel kills only this leg's never-started child (gh-1903).
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903, correlation from #343): correlates
          # OUR run by the child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" —
          # displayTitle is the only distinguisher in the run-list API),
          # newest match in a tight window. Waits READ-ONLY: a child
          # queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is healthy and is
          # never cancelled/re-dispatched; the bounds are build-ios/
          # submit-ios's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 360m.
          # On leg timeout the watcher cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child (gh-1903) — see the leg-header
          # comment for the full invariant.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30);
    # 240m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. Waits are read-only (gh-1903) —
    # no cancel, no re-dispatch, bounded by the child's per-job timeouts
    # (#344) and this leg timeout.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window. Read-only wait (gh-1903): a wedged/queued run
          # is NEVER cancelled or re-dispatched — build-android/submit-
          # android's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 240m are
          # the only bounds; on leg timeout only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child is cancelled.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15); 360m leg ≥ worst-case + margin
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344). A
    # queued child — including one waiting out a sibling's full 150m
    # matrix leg — is NEVER cancelled (gh-1903); the leg timeout bounds
    # the wait and the watcher orphan-cancels only a never-started child.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343):
          # correlates OUR run by the child's run-name
          # ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a concurrent human
          # dispatch is never adopted. A wedged self-hosted run is NEVER
          # cancelled/re-dispatched — the bounds are the build-macos jobs'
          # own 150m server-side timeouts (#344) and this leg's 360m; on
          # leg timeout the watcher orphan-cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started child.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  windows:
    name: 'Leg: Windows app'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 85m (version 20 + windows build 45 +
    # attach 20); 150m leg > worst-case + margin (the addin-leg sizing).
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'windows')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'windows'
        run: |
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-windows.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The child derives the version itself (same latest-tag+1 math as
          # build-macos/build-mobile — all release children derive the SAME
          # next tag). Shared watcher (gh-1903): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name, waits READ-ONLY within the child's own
          # timeout bounds, orphan-cancels only this leg's never-started
          # child on leg timeout.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-windows.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-windows (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15); 180m leg
    # ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could not
    # even fit a healthy child + appear window — the 180m leg is the
    # #351 sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # pages.yml takes no inputs, so there is no displayTitle to
          # disambiguate on — the watcher falls back to
          # newest-in-tight-window and waits read-only: no cancel, no
          # re-dispatch, bounded by the pages jobs' own timeout-minutes
          # (#344) and this leg's 180m.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job); 150m
    # leg ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could
    # not even fit a healthy child + appear window — 150m is the #351
    # sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too

    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, OR the body carries a well-formed
#     `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:
#   stale + pipeline (bot author or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched
drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { bucket: (
          if ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author marker_run; do
  [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
  case "$bucket" in
    fresh)
      fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
      ;;
    human)
      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))
      # Name the creating run so a RECURRING stuck draft points at its
      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name
      # it exactly (the stamping scripts write run/<id>); untagged
      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.
      run_url=""
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ]; then
        run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
      elif [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        run_url=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 1 \
          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi
      [ -n "$run_url" ] || run_url="no run on ref \`$tag\` (dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run)"
      # gh-2105: the staging draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN
      # (ci.yml's push run on the tag ref — release-provenance is the
      # sole publish point, gh-1801). When that train failed, the
      # creating run named above is NOT the broken step — the train is,
      # and a superseded failed train is never rerun
      # (verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only). Name it
      # (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) so the sweep issue points at
      # the true blocker. Any lookup failure degrades to the static
      # prose below — the delete + issue filing must never depend on
      # the diagnosis.
      train_line=""
      if [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
          --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
          --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
        failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
          ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
            | if . == null then empty else
                {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
              end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [ -n "$failed_train" ]; then
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          failed_jobs=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
            | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
          train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
          [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
          train_line="$train_line\n"
        fi
      fi
      deleted="$deleted- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n$train_line"
      deleted_tags="$deleted_tags $tag"
      ;;
  esac
done <<< "$drafts"

# ── issue lifecycle (dedup + self-closing) ─────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # echoes the issue number of the open sweep issue, or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label "$label" \
    --limit 100 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$title" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

stale_count=$((deleted_count + $(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true) ))

if [ "$stale_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  body=$(mktemp)
  {
    echo "**Sweep run:** $daily_url"
    echo "**Swept:** $deleted_count stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than $((max_age / 3600))h"
    printf '%b' "$deleted"
    [ -n "$humans" ] && { echo; echo "**Kept (human drafts, listed not deleted — E1):**"; printf '%b' "$humans"; }
    echo
    echo "**Fresh drafts (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $fresh_count — untouched (an in-flight run may own them)"
    echo
    if [ "$failed_trains" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "**Failed tag trains named above:** $failed_trains"
      echo
      echo "A stale draft whose tag train failed means the publish owner never ran — the draft was the gh-1801 staging draft and release-provenance (its sole publish point) is gated behind the failed train. Rerun the train if the tag should still ship; recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    else
      echo "A stale draft means a \`gh release create\` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step. Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily draft sweeper; auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale."
  } > "$body"
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    issue_action="commented on #$existing (still finding stale drafts)"
  else
    created_issue=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" \
      --body-file "$body" --label bug --label "$label" --assignee ai-teammate 2>/dev/null || true)
    issue_action="filed ${created_issue:-<issue creation failed>}"
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
else
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  issue_action="none needed"
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ sweep found nothing stale — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    issue_action="auto-closed #$existing (clean sweep)"
  fi
fi

# ── job summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{
  echo "### Release-draft sweeper"
  echo
  echo "Deleted **$deleted_count** stale pipeline-created draft(s) • failed tag trains named: **$failed_trains** • kept human drafts: **$(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true)** • fresh (<$((max_age / 3600))h): **$fresh_count** • issue lifecycle: $issue_action"
} >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/stdout}"

echo "sweeper: deleted=${deleted_tags# } human-kept=${human_tags# } fresh=$fresh_count issue=$issue_action"

# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.

String stubGh(String dir) {
  final bin = Directory('$dir/bin')..createSync(recursive: true);
  File('${bin.path}/gh').writeAsStringSync('''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "\$*" >> "\$GH_LOG_FILE"
cmd="\$1"

# Permission enforcement (review of #294): mirror the GITHUB_TOKEN scope
# each subcommand needs, so a workflow forgetting to grant one fails TESTS
# instead of dying silently in production (gh run list 403s without
# actions:read and the sweeper's || true hides the dead "creating run"
# feature). GH_STUB_PERMISSIONS is a space-separated granted-scope list;
# unset means full access.
granted="\${GH_STUB_PERMISSIONS:-*}"
need=""
case "\$cmd \$2" in
  "run list"|"run view"|"run watch"|"run rerun") need=actions ;;
  "issue "*|"label "*) need=issues ;;
  "release "*|"api"*) need=contents ;;
esac
if [ "\$granted" != "*" ] && [ -n "\$need" ] \\
   && ! printf '%s\\n' "\$granted" | grep -qw "\$need"; then
  echo "gh: HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by integration (stub: '\$cmd \$2' needs '\$need'; granted: '\$granted')" >&2
  exit 1
fi

case "\$cmd" in
  api)
    case "\$2 \$3" in
      "-X DELETE"*) : ;;
      *) cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/releases.json" ;;
    esac
    ;;
  label)
    case "\$2" in
      # gh-1134: view succeeds only when the fixture label exists; create
      # self-heals it (unless label-create-fails is planted) — mirrors real
      # GitHub: create is idempotent-failure when the label already exists.
      view) [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/label-exists" ] && exit 0 || exit 1 ;;
      create)
        if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/label-create-fails" ]; then
          echo "gh: label create failed (stub)" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        touch "\$GH_STUB_DIR/label-exists" ;;
      *) : ;;
    esac
    ;;
  pr)
    case "\$2" in
      list)
        if printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--state closed'; then echo 0
        elif printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q 'headRefName'; then echo 0
        else cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/open-pr.txt" 2>/dev/null || true; fi ;;
      *) : ;;
    esac
    ;;
  run)
    if [ "\$2" = "list" ] && printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--workflow'; then
      # gh-2105: the sweeper's tag-train lookup
      # (gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch <tag>) — served from
      # train-runs.json when planted, an empty array otherwise. The
      # plain --branch fallback below must keep hitting runs.tsv (the
      # existing creating-run fixtures).
      if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-runs.json" ]; then
        cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-runs.json"
      else
        echo "[]"
      fi
    elif [ "\$2" = "view" ] && printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--json jobs'; then
      # gh-2105: the failed-train job names (gh run view <id> --json jobs).
      if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-jobs.json" ]; then
        cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/train-jobs.json"
      else
        echo '{"jobs":[]}'
      fi
    elif [ "\$2" = "view" ] && printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q -- '--json status'; then

      # lifecycle status; run-status.json when planted, completed otherwise.
      if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/run-status.json" ]; then
        cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/run-status.json"
      else
        echo '{"status":"completed"}'
      fi
    else
      [ "\$2" = "list" ] && cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/runs.tsv" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    ;;
  issue)
    if [ "\$2" = "list" ]; then cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/issues.tsv" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0; fi
    want_url=""
    [ "\$2" = "create" ] && want_url=1
    while [ \$# -gt 0 ]; do
      if [ "\$1" = "--body-file" ]; then
        cp "\$2" "\$GH_STUB_DIR/last-body.md" 2>/dev/null || true

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2287

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily draft sweeper (`scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`, riding `daily-publish.yml` → `sweep-drafts`) misclassifies stale draft releases authored by the repo's machine account (`ai-teammate`) as "human drafts": they are listed but never deleted, so every daily sweep re-files/comments the same `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` issue with "Swept: 0" — an issue that can never auto-close (the recurrence this ticket captures).

**Root cause**: `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`, the jq bucketing rule (the pipeline-authorship predicate). A stale draft is deleted only when the author is a Bot type, the login ends in `[bot]`, or the body carries the well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/` marker. Drafts created by the ai-teammate automation (tags `ai-gh-<issue>` / `ai-pr-<pr>`, e.g. `ai-gh-2208`, `ai-pr-210`) are authored by `ai-teammate` — a plain `User` login with no `[bot]` suffix, created with the factory's own token, so no marker — and therefore fall into the `human` bucket forever. `ai-teammate` is the machine account in this repo (`ai-teammate.yml` header: the loop reacts only to artifacts authored by `ai-teammate`; every self-filed issue is `--assignee ai-teammate`; `daily_publish_report.sh` already parameterizes the identity as `DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE`, default `ai-teammate`), so these are pipeline-created drafts that rot forever. This is the gh-2008 class of failure (author attribution is not human evidence) with a new vector: the machine's own User-typed account. Because kept human drafts feed `stale_count`, the sweep issue is filed daily and auto-close ("auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale") can never happen while they exist.

**Impact**: (a) machine drafts accumulate unbounded — the ticket's sweep deleted 0 while 4 stale machine drafts and 8 fresh ones were present; (b) recurring daily sweep issue noise that never self-closes; (c) E1's "human drafts are listed, never deleted" safety rule is spent on machine artifacts, muting the signal it was built for (a genuinely human stale draft is now indistinguishable from automation litter in the issue body).

**Fix approach**: teach the bucketing rule the machine-account identity. Add `assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"` to `sweep_stale_drafts.sh` (same env var + default as `daily_publish_report.sh`), pass it into the jq rule as `--arg assignee`, and extend the pipeline predicate with `author.login == $assignee` so a stale machine-account draft is swept like a bot-authored one (fresh ones stay untouched — an in-flight leg may own them; genuinely human drafts stay listed-not-deleted, E1 unchanged). Export `DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate` in the `sweep-drafts` job env so the wiring is explicit and reviewable, and use `$assignee` for the self-filed issue assignee so the machine identity has a single source. For a swept machine draft with no ownership marker, name the machine account as the creator in the issue instead of the misleading "dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run" prose (gh-2105 class: the diagnosis must not misdirect the RCA — nothing "died", the ai-teammate automation loop created it outside this repo's runners).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this recurrence vector.

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" --arg assignee "$assignee" '

    | { bucket: (

          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))

# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║

# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

---

Do **not** guess, hardcode, or fake a passing result. 2. Write `outputs/blocked.json` at the repository root with the exact blocker details: ```json { "reason": "Specific external blocker preventing completion", "tried": ["What was checked or attempted"], "needs": "Exact secret, permission, data, or decision a human must provide" } ``` 3. Do not duplicate its work.** If there ARE concerns: write `outputs/concerns.md` — for each concern: (a) what the PR does, (b) what is missing, (c) concretely what is needed to make it work (exact file names, IDs, console/account steps). Short and factual; the pipeline appends it to the completion comment and the PR body and labels the ticket `ai_concerns`. If there are NO concerns: write nothing — no file, no label. ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md is a PR description — keep it under 20 lines"] F2["Required sections:
### Root Cause
2-3 sentences from rca.md"] F3["### Previous Attempt
PR # and why it failed (only if returned bug)"] F4["### Fix
What changed, in which files, and why"] F5["### Test Coverage
Reproduction test + full suite result"] F6["### Notes
Warnings or assumptions for reviewer"] F7["Use bullet points, not paragraphs. Technical focus only."] F1 --> F2 --> F3 --> F4 --> F5 --> F6 --> F7 ``` ## few_shots.md Example bug fix PR descriptions — follow this structure and brevity: ```mermaid flowchart TD E1["### Root Cause
Null pointer when processing orders without a shipping address. `OrderValidator` assumed `address` field was always present."] E2["### Previous Attempt
PR #142 added a null check in `OrderController`, but the root cause was in `OrderValidator` which runs before the controller."] E3["### Fix
- `OrderValidator.java`: added null-safe address validation with early return
- `OrderValidatorTest.java`: added reproduction test for missing address"] E4["### Test Coverage
- `OrderValidatorTest.shouldRejectOrderWithMissingAddress` — PASSED
- Full suite: 247 tests passed, 0 failures"] E5["### Notes
No breaking changes — existing orders with valid addresses are unaffected."] ``` ## dmtools_cli.md ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY
dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:
dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ## session_ephemerality.md ```mermaid flowchart LR ENV["⚠️ ONE-SHOT SESSION — this agent runs in an ephemeral CI runner.
When your final turn ends, the process EXITS and the runner is destroyed:
- schedule_message / self-reminders NEVER fire after exit — no wake-up exists
- detached processes (nohup/&) are killed with the runner
- nothing can be finished 'later' — there is no later"] ENV --> RULE["NEVER end the session with work pending.

run it in background (bash background:true) and poll with
bash_job status/output BETWEEN your steps — the process stays alive
while you keep working — or run it in the foreground if nothing else
remains. Do NOT arm a timer and exit; do NOT nohup-and-exit."] RULE --> ARTIFACT["The ONLY completion artifact is outputs/response.md

'interrupted mid-way': the ticket resets for retry and the

You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"] C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"] C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"] end subgraph BGJOBS["⚠️ Long-running commands — background execution, never foreground-poll"] B1["Any command that can run longer than ~2 minutes (full test suite, coverage run, build, dependency install, dev server or watch mode) MUST be started with bash background: true — you get a job id immediately and the completion notice arrives as a message"] B2["❌ NEVER wait for a long job with foreground sleep-polling: repeated sleep-then-check loops like sleep 540 → ls coverage. A foreground sleep pins the tool-call open — owner steering and cancel cannot reach you until it ends — and burns wall-clock plus a runner slot"] B3["While a background job runs, keep working on other steps — check progress between steps with bash_job status / bash_job output <job-id> — never park the turn in a watch loop"] B4["A harness hint like background candidate: bash background: true, job board /tasks, --wait-for-jobs is an ORDER, not a suggestion — obey it and start the command in the background; working around it with foreground sleeps is a violation"] B5["Verification order: finalize ALL code edits BEFORE launching a long verification run (full suite, coverage) — verification must run against a frozen tree, otherwise the run is wasted"] B6["Files changed while a verification run is in flight? Do NOT kill it mid-flight — let it finish, treat the result as stale, then deliberately start a fresh run against the updated tree"] B7["B6 covers a job still making progress — do NOT kill it mid-flight; a job with NO progress for ~10 min (or 2× its expected duration) is HUNG — dispose of it and MOVE ON: bash_job stop <job-id>, note the disposal in the deliverable (job id, command, last output tail), finish the remaining steps and write outputs/response.md reporting the unverified part. NEVER let a hung child hold the deliverable hostage: validation CI on the pull request is the safety net"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> B6 --> B7 end USE --> SHELLSTATE SHELLSTATE --> CWD CWD --> BGJOBS ``` ## development-mode-adaptive-appendix.md # Scope estimate & working mode (adaptive dev leg) Before your FIRST code edit: survey the ticket and the relevant code, then estimate the work and fix your working mode for this leg. ## Estimate - One whole number on an open-ended scale: if the work feels bigger than the value you named, keep going. - Estimate EFFORT, RISK and UNCERTAINTY — not file count. A sweeping mechanical rename is low; a small change into undocumented behavior is high. - Structural surprises belong in a higher estimate: data/schema migrations, changes touching a second repository, unknown integration surfaces. - Uncertainty resolves UP: when torn between two values, take the larger. ## Record Write exactly one JSON object to `outputs//scope_estimate.json` ( = the ticket key): {"sp": , "threshold": , "mode": "plan" | "default", "reason": ""} ## Decide (threshold: 3) - sp >= threshold → work BY A PLAN for the rest of this leg: read `.dmtools/development-mode-plan-appendix.md` now and follow its protocol (numbered tasks with what+verify, the committed snapshot, per-task checkpoints). Never demote back to direct mode within the same leg. - sp < threshold → implement directly; no plan artifacts. - Scope grows mid-work and a re-estimate reaches the threshold → raise it: write plan.md, follow the plan protocol from that point, update the record's "mode" to "plan" (and "sp" to the new estimate). ## Complete honestly Before writing `outputs//response.md`, set the record's final "outcome": "completed" | "blocked". A plan-mode leg reports completion only when its plan tasks are done — or honestly marked blocked/deferred in plan.md. ## github_comment_format.md # GitHub tracker comment Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every construct must render natively on GitHub. - Headings: `##`, `###` - Bullets: `- item` - Numbered lists: `1. item` - Bold: `**text**` - Inline code: `` `code` `` - Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`bash`, `json`, `text`) - Link: `[text](url)` - Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row) Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks, no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no `{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable. **IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues, get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER` (the composite key form works directly).

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The daily draft sweeper (`scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`) deletes a stale draft only when its author is a Bot type, a `*[bot]` login, or the body carries the `release-draft-owner:` marker. Drafts created by the ai-teammate automation (`ai-gh-<issue>` / `ai-pr-<pr>` tags) are authored by the repo's **machine account** — a plain User login with no `[bot]` suffix and no marker — so they bucket as "human" and are listed-but-kept forever. Because kept human drafts feed the issue-filing count, the `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` issue re-files daily with `Swept: 0` and can never auto-close.

### Fix

- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: the bucketing rule now also matches the machine-account identity — `DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE` (default `ai-teammate`, the same env + default as `daily_publish_report.sh`), passed into the jq rule. A stale machine-account draft is swept; fresh ones stay untouched (an in-flight leg may own them); genuinely human drafts stay listed-not-deleted (E1 unchanged). Swept machine drafts name the automation account as the creator instead of the misleading "dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run" prose (gh-2105 class). The self-filed issue assignee now uses the same `$assignee` source.
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: the `sweep-drafts` job exports `DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate` so the wiring is explicit.
- With the fix, this ticket's 4 stale drafts sweep on the next daily and the issue auto-closes on the following clean sweep.

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` → `AC2 — sweep_stale_drafts.sh gh-2287: stale drafts authored by the machine account (ai-teammate, plain User login) are swept, not kept as human` — multi-item: `ai-gh-*` + `ai-pr-*` swept, human draft kept (E1), fresh machine draft untouched, look-alike login (`ai-teammate-bot`) NOT matched (exact-match only). Confirmed RED before the fix, GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — 14578 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped.
- End-to-end smoke of the script against this ticket's exact draft inventory: `Swept: 4`, fresh untouched, exit 0.

### Notes

- Assumption (documented in `ai-teammate.yml` + issue-assignee conventions): `ai-teammate` is the machine account, so its stale drafts are pipeline litter, not human work. Human-authored drafts keep E1 protection.
- `git fetch origin` has no network path in this dev sandbox (hung until killed); the completion guard was verified locally: `git log origin/main..HEAD` = `10d80d2` on `ai/gh-2287`.

**gh-2287 — [daily-publish] stale release drafts swept — fixed.**

- **Root cause**: `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` classified stale drafts as pipeline-created only via Bot-type author, `*[bot]` login, or a `release-draft-owner:` marker. The ai-teammate automation's drafts (`ai-gh-<issue>`/`ai-pr-<pr>`) are authored by the repo's machine account — plain User login, no marker — so they bucketed as "human", were never deleted, and the sweep issue re-filed daily with `Swept: 0`, never auto-closing.
- **Fix**: the bucketing rule now also matches the machine-account identity (`DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE`, default `ai-teammate` — same env + default as `daily_publish_report.sh`; exported by the `sweep-drafts` job); swept machine drafts name the automation account instead of the misleading "dispatch-time" prose; human drafts keep E1 protection; exact-login match verified against look-alike logins.
- **TDD**: reproduction test confirmed RED first, GREEN after; full suite green.
